chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, said:

In the book of Hariz, he said: 'I forgot that I was in a obligatory prayer until I bowed, while I was intending it as voluntary.' He said, so he said: 'It is the one you stood in. If you stood intending an obligatory prayer, then doubt entered you, then you are in the obligatory prayer. And if you entered a voluntary prayer and intended it as obligatory, then you are in the voluntary prayer. And if you entered an obligatory prayer, then remembered a voluntary prayer that was upon you, then continue in the obligatory prayer.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when a Muslim forgets whether they are praying an obligatory or voluntary prayer?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on *Sahw* (forgetfulness), this narration from Hariz elucidates the principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) in resolving doubt between obligatory and voluntary prayers. It establishes that uncertainty regarding the initial intention defaults to the obligatory status, while remembering a missed voluntary prayer during an obligatory one does not interrupt the current act, reflecting the Shia juristic preference for stability in worship.
